bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client and geographic concentration (growth risk) — Most revenues are derived from a few large US and UK-based clients, so any economic slowdown or downturn in these economies and industries may affect the business. Healthcare services are less prone to recessionary cycles, but the customer-management business is relatively low-margin and more prone to economic variation, and technology disruption could cause volume shrinkage. Mitigated by building differentiated, productised digital services anchored by Intelligence That Operates and Kairos to retain and grow wallet share and win new logos.
- Country, geopolitical and legislative risk - including the proposed US HIRE Act — Operations span India, the US, the UK, the Philippines, Mexico, South Africa, Australia, Dubai (UAE) and Egypt, exposing the Company to geopolitical and regulatory risks beyond its control. The proposed US HIRE Act, which contemplates a 25% tax on payments made by US companies to foreign service providers including Indian IT and BPO companies, is flagged as a legislative risk to monitor, alongside US-India trade tensions spilling into services. Mitigated by local management teams and a well-diversified geographic spread.
- Highly competitive BPS market — Competitors include third-party pure-play BPS providers in India and the Philippines, local/onshore providers in the US and UK, BPS divisions of global IT companies, and in-house captives of potential clients. The Company counters through investment in domain expertise, digital capabilities, process excellence, operational rigour and the Kairos-anchored transformation framework to enable non-linear growth in revenues and margins.
- Non-renewal of key client contracts — Client contracts run between one and ten years, and after a term expires contracts are typically re-tendered through a procurement process; non-renewal may significantly affect revenues.
- Long selling cycle — The BPS selling cycle ranges from months to multiple years and requires significant capital, resources and time from both clients and the Company, delaying revenue conversion. Mitigated by marketing, sales and business-development teams across geographies and an aggressive transition methodology that moves new wins quickly into service delivery.
- Currency volatility (INR vs USD and GBP) — Exchange rates have been volatile and operating results will continue to be impacted; the Indian rupee steadily weakened against the US dollar over 2025, depreciating by approximately 4-5%. A weaker rupee initially boosts revenue realisations, but prolonged instability could raise import costs for IT-related infrastructure. Mitigated by a dedicated treasury function and an internal FX risk management policy that hedges net exposures through forward cover contracts and other suitable products.
- Customer credit, liquidity and solvency risk — Possible inability to collect from clients or delays in collection, with pressure persisting from liquidity situations at certain clients, could affect cash receivables and require temporary enhancement of short-term credit lines. The Company also operates through legal entities in multiple countries subject to differing accounting standards and uses financial leverage, making timely borrowing, repayment and cost of funds important; mitigated by a well-defined governance mechanism and a robust internal financial controls framework.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy — Identified in the BRSR as both a risk and an opportunity - cyberattacks and data-breach incidents threaten data safety, privacy and reputational standing, with potential fines for non-compliance. Mitigated through ISO 27001 certified operation centers with processes certified under HIPAA, HITRUST and SOC2, regular audits with a zero-tolerance policy, secure VPN with two-factor authentication, EDR/DLP/encryption/DNS-layer security and secure mail gateway, third-party vulnerability and penetration testing, PCI DSS compliance scans, source-code and cloud reviews, and 24x7x365 monitoring via MDR services.
- ESG performance and disclosure risk — Inability to demonstrate the outcomes of the ESG programme - covering climate change, GHG reductions, responsible supply chains and governance - can adversely impact operations, reputation and stakeholder trust, and expectations may shift with evolving regulatory and stakeholder requirements. Mitigated by the FirstConscious ESG governance framework aligned to Enterprise Risk Management, with review and reporting to the Board-level Risk Management Committee and an annual review of the materiality assessment.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Firstsource is an asset-light services business, so expansion is expressed through delivery footprint, acquisitions and platform build rather than plants or capacity lines. During FY26 the Company extended its operations to take the global footprint to twelve countries across 57 centers, with 36,205 employees representing 94 nationalities, operating across the US, UK, India, Philippines, Mexico, Romania, Trinidad & Tobago, South Africa, Australia, Canada, Turkey and UAE; the workforce grew 4.5% from 34,651 at March 31, 2025 through a combination of organic and inorganic expansion, including extension of the geographic footprint to the UAE and Egypt. Of the 57 global operation centers as on March 31, 2026, 20 are in India - Chennai (4), Mumbai (4), Coimbatore (3), Bangalore (3) and 1 each in Trichy, Pondicherry, Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Gurugram and Jaipur - with 18 in North America, 14 in EMEA, 4 in the Philippines and 1 in Australia. Capital expenditure during the year was incurred mainly towards refurbishment and maintenance of operation centers, technology upgrade and setting up of new operations centers; the Registered Office was also shifted within Mumbai to 1st Floor, Athena Towers, Mindspace Malad, Goregaon (West). Capability expansion came through two acquisitions - Pastdue Credit Solutions Limited (UK white-label early arrears and debt collections) for GBP 22 million and TeleMedik (US clinical management, utilization review and bilingual care management) for up to US$ 3 million, neither made for scale, both for capability - and through platform build-out, with three significant launches during the year: the Agentic AI Studio, the Gigsourcing Platform and the Mortgage Language Model, which now processes over two million mortgage loans annually across all 50 US states via Sourcepoint, the Company's US mortgage arm. Kairos was rolled out as the digital delivery anchor across Healthcare Payer engagements, with more than 100 prebuilt models and 60 solution accelerators in active deployment.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Industry pivot from AI experimentation to industrialisation - NASSCOM's Strategic Review 2026 characterises the period as the technology industry's third inflection point, the decisive pivot to enterprise AI
- Commercial constructs shifting from input-based pricing to outcome-linked, risk-sharing models as AI-driven productivity gains materialise
- Sector growth driven less by headcount addition than by productivity uplift - a structural change favouring providers operating non-linear, intelligence-led delivery models
- Value creation shifting from labor arbitrage to intelligence arbitrage; enterprises reward partners who compound value, learning and outcomes rather than scale alone
- The gap between AI ambition and AI in production has become the defining boardroom issue, widening the performance spread between enterprises that re-architected operating models and those layering AI onto legacy stacks
- Intensifying regulatory complexity raises the premium on partners combining deep domain expertise with auditable, governed automation; governance has become a differentiator rather than a compliance burden
- BFS: elevated interest rates, deposit pressure and regulatory complexity; Europe transaction volumes subdued with slower digital transformation than North America, where consumer lending, mortgage services and fintech innovation provide a more resilient demand backdrop; accelerating GenAI, cloud and analytics adoption across lending, payments, servicing, compliance, fraud, document processing and workflow automation
- Healthcare: US health plan margin pressure from elevated Medicare utilization, payment-rate constraints and inflation fuels demand for intelligent operations, BPaaS and AI-enabled decision support; provider financial stress and clinical-workforce shortages accelerate the shift to technology-led RCM platforms
- CMT: convergence of traditional and digital-first players, consumer technology companies leading GenAI deployment, and telecom/media focus on modernising legacy systems and cost efficiency; supporting AI-native businesses at scale plays to strengths in AI and analytics
- Diverse Industries: utilities customer-service transformation driven by regulatory focus on billing accuracy, service responsiveness and vulnerable-customer management; retail extended through Ascensos nearshore multilingual CX
- Margin levers identified and in execution: right-shoring, automation, process excellence, account-level margin improvement, talent cost rationalization, attrition reduction, and facility optimization
- Attrition closed the year at 29.7%, a meaningful improvement from the highs of previous years, supporting cost and delivery stability
- Outcome-based pricing moving beyond pilots and multi-tower, cross-border mandates becoming the norm as clients engage to redesign how operations perform
- Closing deal pipeline crossed the US$ 1 billion mark, with large deals characteristically multi-tower, cross-border and structured around outcomes rather than inputs
- 17 large deals closed during FY26
- 47 new logos added during FY26, including 24 strategic logos - doubling strategic-account additions versus FY25
- Largest-ever healthcare contract won - a transformation-led mandate with one of America's largest healthcare organizations covering claims at scale, the compliance burden, and the decisions that touch patients' lives
- Most contracts with existing clients are long-term, ensuring sustainable and scalable business

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Firstsource Solutions, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, is a global intelligence partner to enterprises across Healthcare, Banking and Financial Services, Communications, Media and Technology, Retail and Utilities, positioned on the promise of "Intelligence That Operates".

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Firstsource combines deep domain expertise built over twenty-five years with an agent-first delivery model to transform, implement and operate intelligent enterprise operations spanning the full customer lifecycle. Rather than acting as a back-office vendor, the Company is increasingly engaged as a partner that advises, implements, runs and transforms in one continuous motion, with accountability for the outcome; this is operationalised through Kairos, its operating system for AI-native operations that encodes domain expertise as executable know-how, governance guardrails and continuous-learning loops. It serves clients through four reportable verticals - Banking and Financial Services, Healthcare, Communications, Media and Technology, and Diverse Industries (Utilities, Retail and other emerging segments) - each combining domain expertise with vertical-native AI platforms operated under the Kairos model.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industry pivot from AI experimentation to industrialisation - NASSCOM's Strategic Review 2026 characterises the period as the technology industry's third inflection point, the decisive pivot to enterprise AI
- Commercial constructs shifting from input-based pricing to outcome-linked, risk-sharing models as AI-driven productivity gains materialise
- Sector growth driven less by headcount addition than by productivity uplift - a structural change favouring providers operating non-linear, intelligence-led delivery models
- Value creation shifting from labor arbitrage to intelligence arbitrage; enterprises reward partners who compound value, learning and outcomes rather than scale alone
- The gap between AI ambition and AI in production has become the defining boardroom issue, widening the performance spread between enterprises that re-architected operating models and those layering AI onto legacy stacks
- Intensifying regulatory complexity raises the premium on partners combining deep domain expertise with auditable, governed automation; governance has become a differentiator rather than a compliance burden
- BFS: elevated interest rates, deposit pressure and regulatory complexity; Europe transaction volumes subdued with slower digital transformation than North America, where consumer lending, mortgage services and fintech innovation provide a more resilient demand backdrop; accelerating GenAI, cloud and analytics adoption across lending, payments, servicing, compliance, fraud, document processing and workflow automation
- Healthcare: US health plan margin pressure from elevated Medicare utilization, payment-rate constraints and inflation fuels demand for intelligent operations, BPaaS and AI-enabled decision support; provider financial stress and clinical-workforce shortages accelerate the shift to technology-led RCM platforms
- CMT: convergence of traditional and digital-first players, consumer technology companies leading GenAI deployment, and telecom/media focus on modernising legacy systems and cost efficiency; supporting AI-native businesses at scale plays to strengths in AI and analytics
- Diverse Industries: utilities customer-service transformation driven by regulatory focus on billing accuracy, service responsiveness and vulnerable-customer management; retail extended through Ascensos nearshore multilingual CX
- Margin levers identified and in execution: right-shoring, automation, process excellence, account-level margin improvement, talent cost rationalization, attrition reduction, and facility optimization
- Attrition closed the year at 29.7%, a meaningful improvement from the highs of previous years, supporting cost and delivery stability
- Outcome-based pricing moving beyond pilots and multi-tower, cross-border mandates becoming the norm as clients engage to redesign how operations perform
- Closing deal pipeline crossed the US$ 1 billion mark, with large deals characteristically multi-tower, cross-border and structured around outcomes rather than inputs
- 17 large deals closed during FY26
- 47 new logos added during FY26, including 24 strategic logos - doubling strategic-account additions versus FY25
- Largest-ever healthcare contract won - a transformation-led mandate with one of America's largest healthcare organizations covering claims at scale, the compliance burden, and the decisions that touch patients' lives
- Most contracts with existing clients are long-term, ensuring sustainable and scalable business

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Firstsource is an asset-light services business, so expansion is expressed through delivery footprint, acquisitions and platform build rather than plants or capacity lines. During FY26 the Company extended its operations to take the global footprint to twelve countries across 57 centers, with 36,205 employees representing 94 nationalities, operating across the US, UK, India, Philippines, Mexico, Romania, Trinidad & Tobago, South Africa, Australia, Canada, Turkey and UAE; the workforce grew 4.5% from 34,651 at March 31, 2025 through a combination of organic and inorganic expansion, including extension of the geographic footprint to the UAE and Egypt. Of the 57 global operation centers as on March 31, 2026, 20 are in India - Chennai (4), Mumbai (4), Coimbatore (3), Bangalore (3) and 1 each in Trichy, Pondicherry, Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Gurugram and Jaipur - with 18 in North America, 14 in EMEA, 4 in the Philippines and 1 in Australia. Capital expenditure during the year was incurred mainly towards refurbishment and maintenance of operation centers, technology upgrade and setting up of new operations centers; the Registered Office was also shifted within Mumbai to 1st Floor, Athena Towers, Mindspace Malad, Goregaon (West). Capability expansion came through two acquisitions - Pastdue Credit Solutions Limited (UK white-label early arrears and debt collections) for GBP 22 million and TeleMedik (US clinical management, utilization review and bilingual care management) for up to US$ 3 million, neither made for scale, both for capability - and through platform build-out, with three significant launches during the year: the Agentic AI Studio, the Gigsourcing Platform and the Mortgage Language Model, which now processes over two million mortgage loans annually across all 50 US states via Sourcepoint, the Company's US mortgage arm. Kairos was rolled out as the digital delivery anchor across Healthcare Payer engagements, with more than 100 prebuilt models and 60 solution accelerators in active deployment.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
